tree.t: Incidental gallbladder or biliary finding on CT or MRI

c.t:
No routine follow-up
Individualize to
comorbidity; use
contrast CT if followed

MRCP, EUS, or ERCP
(EUS-FNA for a distal
CBD mass)

note: * Short-axis CBD or common hepatic duct > 6 mm in a patient < 60 years with the gallbladder present, or > 10 mm after cholecystectomy; > 7 mm suggests obstruction with the gallbladder in place. Mild dilation with normal labs needs no further imaging.
cite: Sebastian S et al. Managing Incidental Findings on Abdominal and Pelvic CT and MRI, Part 4: White Paper of the ACR Incidental Findings Committee II on Gallbladder and Biliary Findings. J Am Coll Radiol. 2013;10(12):953-956.
